messages:
incident-bot: Alert — elevated 502/504 rate detected at apigw-us-west-2. 3-minute rolling error rate: 18%. Latency spike on L7 edge.

ingress-oncall: I'm on it. Confirming pager. Any deploys in the last 15m?

Sanjay (eng-runtime): No infra deploys from runtime in last 30m. We pushed a model artifact to dedicated late last night but that's unrelated.

Katie (prod-resp): I'm seeing increased errors correlated with requests that include large request bodies (batch embeddings route). 50% of failing traces have X-Forwarded-Proto missing.

Dena (support): Customer impact: several enterprise customers reporting failed requests and timeouts. Support opened 4 tickets. Marking high.

Miguel (sre-lead): Quick plan: 1) throttle large-body routes at the gateway for now 2) enable regional fallback to eu-west-1 for affected customers 3) check proxy pool exhaustion 4) gate rolling deploys.

ingress-oncall: Trying a temp rule to 429 large-body requests to reduce fanout. Running:

```
kubectl exec -it gw-proxy-0 -- curl -sS localhost:9000/metrics | grep conn_pool
```

Got: conn_pool_errors: 1200

Sanjay (eng-runtime): conn pool errors look like upstream timeouts causing many 502s. Could be an upstream (inference) node hotspot that trips connection reuse. Flushing upstream KV cache and restarting a single problematic proxy pod to see if it clears.

Katie (prod-resp): I'm going to enable a temporary circuit-breaker in the route config for /v1/embeddings/batch and reduce max_connections to 50. Will post the change.

ingress-oncall: Patch applied, returning 200 on health check for changed pod. Observability: error rate dropped to 10% after patch, but customer-facing requests still impacted.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: oncall acknowledged by ingress-oncall.

Dena (support): Notifying impacted customers with a short advisory: "We are investigating intermittent 502/504 errors for batch embedding requests in us-west-2. Temporary mitigations in progress." Sending now.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Rolling restart of gw-proxy-2 in progress to clear sticky keepalives. Command: `kubectl rollout restart ds/gw-proxy -n infra --field-selector metadata.name=gw-proxy-2`

Miguel (sre-lead): Also spinning up 2 additional proxy workers as short-term capacity increase. If this stabilizes, we'll keep them for 15m then scale down.

ingress-oncall: After restart and circuit-breaker, 502/504 rate steady at ~4% over 3m windows. Latency normalized.

Katie (prod-resp): Rolling map of customers: we shifted 60% of traffic to eu-west fallback for critical customers (IDs sent in DM). Remaining customers see degraded but usable responses.

Dena (support): All four opened tickets updated. One large customer requested ETA; replied with mitigation summary and asked to escalate if errors persist.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: an upstream inference shard lost connection pool slots under a sudden batch request pattern, causing upstream resets and gateway 502s. Need deeper postmortem. I'll capture heap/conn metrics from affected nodes.

Miguel (sre-lead): Action items: 1) keep circuit-breaker enabled for batch route 2) run a controlled load test on staging with large batch bodies to reproduce 3) schedule a 1-hour postmortem after incident closes 4) Owner: Sanjay for root cause, Katie for customer comms.

ingress-oncall: I'm handing off to night oncall in 20m. Handoff note: circuit-breaker active, two extra proxy workers up, regional fallback enabled for critical customers, support notified.

incident-bot: Handoff logged. Next oncall: Tom (ingress-night).

Katie (prod-resp): Thanks team. I'll draft the incident advisory for the status page and include mitigation steps.

Dena (support): Closing loop with support team; will reopen if errors exceed 5% in next 30m.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Collecting logs and connection metrics (tcp_retransmits, keepalive resets) and uploading to /shared/incidents/3032105550/ for the postmortem.

Miguel (sre-lead): Good work. Keep monitoring. If error rate creeps above 6% re-escalate immediately.

ingress-oncall: 14m in, error rate 3.6%. Handing off now. :thumbsup:
